blocks.text:
ק׳ תַּאֲלַת זוּ כְּחֵפֶץ לְהַתְעִיל. שׁוּעַ עֲרוֹךְ
לְמָרֹם לְהוֹעִיל. רוֹן הַרְרֵי קֶדֶם הַמּוֹעִיל.
קְרוֹא בְּגָרוֹן מוֹקֵשׁ לְהַגְעִיל: צִדְקָם לְהַקְפּוֹת
בְּנִיב שַׁוְעָה. פָּעֳלָם בְּקֶרֶב שָׁנִים לְשָׁמְעָה.
עֵת רָצוֹן וְיוֹם יְשׁוּעָה. סְבִיכַת קֶרֶן וּבְרִית
שְׁבוּעָה: נוֹבְבִים בְּגִשַּׁת חוֹתָמוֹת תִּשְׁעָה.
מִסְפַּר שָׁתוֹת וְחוֹתְמֵיהֶן תִּשְׁעָה. לְמִנְיַן פִּלּוּל
שֵׁמוֹת תִּשְׁעָה. כְּחַנָּה עֲקָרָה יָלְדָה שִׁבְעָה:
יַאֲמִירוּ עֹז מַלְכִיּוֹת עֶשֶׂר. טְבוּעוֹת לְשֵׁם
כֹּהֵן בְּעֶשֶׂר. חֹק זִכְרוֹנוֹת וְקוֹלוֹת עֶשֶׂר.
זֵכֶר מְבָרֵךְ גְּבִיר (נ״א גְּבִירוֹ) בְּעֶשֶׂר: וַיִּפֶן בְּאָהוּב
אֲתוּי נַהֲרַיִם. הֶעָקוּד בְּהַר מוֹר אֲחוֹרַיִם.
דִּשְׁנוּ יָרֵא לָחֹן שִׁירִים. גָּשִׁים עָדָיו כְּבֹקֶר
וְצָהֳרָיִם: בְּזֶה פֶּרֶק חֲנַן עֲתִירָה. בְּעַד אֲסוּרָה
עַד הֻתְּרָה. ק׳ אֶנְקַת אָסִיר אָז כְּהִכְתִּירָה.
אֵלִי לְהֵעָתֵר כְּמוֹ נֶעְתָּרָה:
blocks.location: band1 line 1 through band4 line 4. The paragraph is indented and opens with a small ק׳. A second small ק׳ appears mid-line before אֶנְקַת. Line breaks follow the print. Band3's bottom line and band4's top line are the same printed lines, cut by the band edge: the tops of 'וְצָהֳרָיִם… בְּעַד אֲסוּרָה' and the bottoms of 'דִּשְׁנוּ… כְּבֹקֶר'. No printed line is missing between the bands.

blocks.text:
ק׳ מֶלֶךְ בְּדִין עֲלוֹת בִּתְרוּעָה. גֵּיא עַם
דָּרֶיהָ לְרוֹעָה. ק׳ בַּשּׁוֹפָר ([?] שבת בְּזִכְרוֹן שׁוֹפָר)
אַפְּתֵנוּ: (נ״א אַרְצֵנוּ) וּבְבֶרֶךְ כְּרִיעָה. בְּטַלְלֵי
תְּחִי בְּגַנּוֹ אֶתְרוֹעֲעָה:
blocks.location: band4 line 5 to band5 line 2. New indented paragraph opening with a small ק׳, with another small ק׳ before בַּשּׁוֹפָר. Both parentheticals are set in small Rashi-type: the Shabbat substitution after בַּשּׁוֹפָר, and the variant before וּבְבֶרֶךְ.
band5 below the last line: blank, with no footer or catchword visible

uncertain.word: [?] (first token of the parenthetical after בַּשּׁוֹפָר)
uncertain.uncertainty: It is a small Rashi-type token of about two letters and looks like חַמ / חַס with a patach. I can't settle it: it may be an abbreviation such as 'וּבְ' or 'בש׳'. Only שבת בְּזִכְרוֹן שׁוֹפָר after it is clear.

uncertain.word: נ״א (×2: before גְּבִירוֹ and before אַרְצֵנוּ)
uncertain.location: band3 line 4; band4 line 7 / band5 line 1
uncertain.uncertainty: In Rashi-type the first letter looks like כ (כ״א). I read it as Rashi נ, giving נ״א. The glyph alone is ambiguous between כ and נ.
The vowel on the vav is unclear: holam or shuruk (עֲרוּךְ). The mark under ע also looks like a hataf patach rather than a kamatz, which is unexpected.
The consonants are ל־מ־ר־ם, with no vav. The vowels under or over מ and ר (kamatz or holam) aren't clearly resolved.
There are marks under ה and the first ר. They could be read as הֲרָרֵי, but the scan doesn't resolve them clearly.
The mark under ק looks like sheva. Kamatz is not excluded.
There is an extra small mark around the ג (geresh-like or a dagesh fleck).
The dagesh in פ is uncertain.
The second letter (after the vav) could be ב or כ (נוֹכְבִים). I read ב.
The first letter could be ח or ה. The left leg seems joined, which would make it ח, but this is not certain.
The vowel under ש could be kamatz or sheva (שְׁתוֹת).
I can't confirm a holam dot on the ע.
The vowel under ה could be tsere or patach.
The vowel under the initial ו could be patach or sheva, and the dagesh in י is unclear.
The vav could be shuruk or holam.
In both words I can't settle whether the yod carries a hiriq (‑ַיִם) or the ending is plain ‑ִים. The vowels under נ and ה in נַהֲרַיִם are also unclear.
The first letter could be ד or ר. I read ד with a dagesh.
The first letter could be כ or ב, the vowel under it could be sheva or patach (כַּבֹּקֶר), and the dagesh in ב is unclear. The line is cut at the band edge.
The final letter could be ד or ר (בְּעַר).
The vowel under ח could be hataf patach or hiriq.
The vowel under ת (sheva or kamatz) and the dagesh are uncertain.
The vowels under ט and the first ל, and whether the second ל has a dagesh, are uncertain.
The vowel under ת could be sheva or tsere.
The vowel under א (hataf patach or patach) and the dagesh in פ are uncertain.

coverage_limits: This reading uses only the five supplied bands. No repository text or earlier report was consulted. Where bands overlap, the cut lines were matched to each other, and I found no lost line. The resolution is too low to settle every small vowel point and dagesh; the main doubts are listed under 'uncertain', and other minor pointing has not been verified mark by mark. The Rashi-type parentheticals are the least reliable, especially the first token of the Shabbat substitution. Only the upper part of page 50 is shown; I can't tell whether text continues beyond band5, which ends in blank space.
